passage: I'm Bidisha, and my window faces Tushar's balcony, so I saw his last fortnight before the entrance test. First he was up at all hours, pacing with sheets of paper, muttering formulas. On Tuesday he stopped opening new chapters. He began taking a twenty-minute walk around the block at six, and his light went off by ten. On the balcony he carried only one sheet, a page of formulas, instead of the pile. I can't know whether he was scared. He went quiet, and I did see him stand still with his eyes closed for a minute. By Friday he was humming while he watered the plants.

qa.q: What did Tushar carry on the balcony in the last days?
qa.a: Only one sheet with a page of formulas.

qa.q: What might Tushar have been feeling when he stopped opening new chapters?
qa.a: Anxious, but deciding to protect his energy; Bidisha cannot be sure, but the pacing before and humming later suggest worry easing.

qa.q: What else could Tushar do if the worry spikes at night, and why?
qa.a: Tell a parent, sibling or counsellor about it, since saying it aloud may ease it and an adult can help him plan.

qa.q: How does Tushar's change look from Bidisha's window?
qa.a: Bidisha sees the pacing, then a calmer routine, but cannot know what Tushar felt inside, so the humming is only a hint.

passage:
Day 1, a Monday, fourteen days before the entrance exam: Asif woke at 4 am with his heart racing and couldn't sleep again. At breakfast his hands shook holding the cup. He'd planned three new chapters that week. His sister Arohi noticed him staring at the same page. "You okay?" "No," he admitted. "Everything feels like it's slipping."

Day 3, Wednesday: He'd decided. "No new topics now," he told Arohi. "Only revision." He made formula sheets for each subject, one page each. Every evening at six he walked for twenty minutes around the colony park. Lights off by ten-thirty, phone in the kitchen.

Day 12, the Friday before the exam: He was reading his formula sheets on the balcony, calm enough to laugh at a joke Arohi made. "My brain feels like it has space again," he said. On Sunday he walked into the exam hall rested.

qa.q: What time did Asif walk every evening?
qa.a: At six, for twenty minutes around the colony park.

qa.q: How did Asif feel on day 1?
qa.a: He felt anxious and panicky, heart racing and hands shaking, as if everything was slipping.

qa.q: What else could Asif do if anxiety spikes on exam morning?
qa.a: He could take a few slow breaths and glance over one formula sheet, and tell a family member if the anxiety stays high.

qa.q: How might Arohi have seen her brother's change over the two weeks?
qa.a: Arohi likely felt relieved, watching him go from staring at one page to laughing and feeling calmer.

grounding: Shows a teen noticing anxiety spiking in the last fortnight, stopping new topics, walking, sleeping on time and switching to light revision of formula sheets.

passage:
Bidisha, you're trying to learn three new chapters in your last two weeks? Sit. Let your Omkar dadu tell you about the week my head nearly exploded.

I was seventeen, preparing for the engineering entrance in Nagpur. Two weeks before, I started waking at night with my heart pounding. I couldn't eat properly. I kept opening new chapters, thinking, what if they ask this?

My mother found me at 2 am with a textbook. She took it gently out of my hands. "Enough new things. Your mind needs to settle, not stuff more in."

So I stopped. I wrote one page of formulas for each subject. Every evening I walked to the river and back. I slept by ten.

The last week, I only read those pages. On the exam day, the formulas were right there in my head, clear. The new chapters never mattered.

How did young Omkar feel two weeks before the exam?
qa.a: He felt anxious and restless, waking with his heart pounding and unable to eat properly.

qa.q: What turning point in the story changed his last two weeks, and why?
qa.a: His mother taking the textbook at 2 am was the turning point; it pushed him to stop new chapters and settle his mind with light revision.

qa.q: How might Omkar's mother have felt finding him at 2 am?
qa.a: She was probably worried and protective, which is why she gently took the book and urged rest.

grounding: An elder recalls noticing anxiety spiking before an exam, stopping new topics, walking and sleeping on time, and switching to light revision of formula sheets.
